title: P1-03 — OpenCode 2.2.5 TUI and exit-confirm compatibility
objective: P1-03 TUI compatibility and exit confirmation. Successor to #49/#51; starts after P1-01 ticket #53; compatibility findings inform P1-02 ticket #54, while guest integration/acceptance depends on #54. Timebox investigation before any port. Operating policy: docs/workflows/phase1-continuous-execution.md; M1→M2→M3 is a priority order, not a blocker to independent offline M2 implementation. Reuse settled pinned 2.2.5 probes; continue protected config, plugin and tmux integration without claiming live guest behavior or repeating compatibility tests absent contradictory evidence.

acceptance_criteria.text: Timebox source/runtime compatibility investigation against pinned OpenCode 2.2.5 before porting; record verified behavior and stop for owner/Sol decision if compatibility or security boundaries are unclear.

Use supported native keybindings when they provide the approved behavior; verify Ctrl+C opens confirmation, Escape/N/Ctrl+C cancel, Y/Q confirm, and Ctrl+D behavior on the pinned binary without losing workspace data.

Any plugins/config are version-pinned, baked into the protected guest and inaccessible for workspace replacement; hostile project config/plugin discovery cannot override protected settings or load an unapproved plugin.

Verify update, telemetry, remote model-list, and sharing behavior under the existing egress policy; keep autoupdate/sharing disabled as configured and do not broaden the allowlist without owner approval.
Document target-terminal clipboard-write mitigation, verify it with a harmless clipboard canary, and state residual terminal-control risks; do not treat SSH EscapeChar=none as a clipboard defense.

needed: Timeboxed OpenCode 2.2.5 TUI/plugin/keybinding/config-precedence probe in an isolated disposable environment.

comments.body: 2026-11-15 hosted SSH root-cause/fix follow-up: owner-provided candidate 429621a evidence was , repeated ssh.service failures while ssh.socket listened on 0.0.0.0:22; cloud-init displayed host-key information later. Source inspection of the pinned cloud-init 26.1 cloud.cfg.tmpl confirms its ssh module runs in cloud_init_modules (init stage) before config-stage runcmd/scripts-user. The CI runner was opening the forwarded SSH port immediately during boot, allowing ssh.socket to activate ssh.service before cloud-init had installed the per-instance keys; repeated failed activations could leave the unit start-limited. Fix gates all initial SSH probes on a guest marker emitted only after ssh-keygen -A (fills missing per-instance keys without replacing existing ones), Ed25519 private-key parse check, sshd -t, and systemd reset-failed. It retains ssh.socket activation, does not print private keys, and uses the existing host-generated unique per-run key with ssh_deletekeys=false. Readiness now requires the strict pre-pinned known_hosts SSH identity to authenticate and the remote command to confirm ssh.service active; the post-reboot strict SSH probe checks service activity too, verifying persisted identity. No disk, timeout, workflow, KVM, cleanup, or persistent-parent change. Local validation: Bats 106/106, ci-kvm-launch 1/1, synthetic OAuth 18/18, browser-auth 37/37, generated cloud-config/embedded shell syntax, bash -n, ShellCheck and diff checks pass. Sol Medium review PASS. No local QEMU/KVM run. Hosted confirmation pending owner push; A1-A5 remain pending.

comments.author: cli
comments.body: 2026-11-15 follow-up to hosted candidate a0624a133cf888b44a42e848eb413cb28dc538d0: hosted failure was KVM_GUEST_SSH_HOSTKEY_FAIL stage=ed25519-private-unusable; cloud-init later emitted ED25519 host-key fingerprints. The old marker only showed ssh-keygen -y returned failure; it did not record whether the private file was absent, mode/owner incorrect, or malformed, so the exact private-key failure cannot be distinguished from that run. Source inspection of cloud-init 26.1 cc_ssh confirms ssh_deletekeys removes image-provided host keys, then ssh_genkeytypes generates requested key types during cloud_init_modules; cc_keys_to_console later emits an SSH HOST KEY KEYS block containing public keys. Ubuntu ssh.socket can be listening before an sshd handshake, so listener state alone is not readiness. Current Change A replaces injected host private-key cloud-config with native per-instance cloud-init Ed25519 generation (ssh_deletekeys=true, ssh_genkeytypes=[ed25519], ssh_quiet_keygen=true), records only private-key metadata and bounded ssh-keygen error text if diagnostics are needed, and waits for cloud-init final completion before extracting one validated public Ed25519 key from the marked serial block and pinning it in strict known_hosts. SSH readiness then requires the actual forwarded authenticated strict-key SSH command, active ssh.service, successful cloud-init and provisioning markers. cloud-init runs once per instance on the same overlay; reboot keeps that generated private key and strict pinned identity. No local/nested QEMU or push. Local checks: Bats 106/106, ci-kvm-launch 1/1, synthetic OAuth 18/18, browser-auth 37/37, host-key parser 4/4, generated cloud-config and embedded shell syntax, bash -n, ShellCheck and diff checks pass. Hosted validation of this correction is NOT_RUN and required before Change B. A1-A5 remain pending.

comments.author: cli
comments.body: Sol Medium technical design for Change B (planning only; no implementation or KVM evidence): retain one real-KVM job, runner, disposable guest and overlay, but expose lifecycle through separate named Actions steps: prepare; start and verify readiness; security/configuration tests; synthetic OAuth; OpenCode/tmux/TUI/reconnect; restricted reboot/persistence; always-run sanitized diagnostics and cleanup. Current tests/ci-kvm-capability.sh owns QEMU, OAuth harness, private temp state and an EXIT trap; that trap cannot span Actions step shells. A minimal detached test-owned supervisor must own/reap QEMU across steps and enforce a watchdog expiry, with atomic mode-0600 versioned private state under mode-0700 RUNNER_TEMP. Every operation must validate run/boot identity, phase prerequisites, QEMU/supervisor UID/parent/start-time/argv, overlay device+inode, loopback port and strict known_hosts/key identity; reboot reuses overlay and records new QEMU identity. Never export keys, cloud-config, auth fixtures, raw argv or state as outputs/artifacts; only a non-secret run locator/status may cross Actions outputs. Carry existing absolute stage/overall deadlines and reserve cleanup time. Use always() cleanup as best effort plus supervisor expiry for cancellation/hard runner loss; report cleanup ambiguity and retain private evidence fail-closed. Preserve existing smoke, security/config, strict host-key, synthetic OAuth descendant cleanup, TUI/reconnect, reboot/persistence, provenance and offline signal/identity coverage; add offline tests for state tamper, identity substitution, deadlines, prerequisites and cleanup failure. Planning only; implementation stays blocked until Change A has complete green hosted real-KVM evidence. A1-A5 remain pending.

That is a harness/runtime-context mismatch worth correcting; hosted output alone does not establish whether it is the sole cause. Local installed @opencode/cli package metadata is 2.2.5; target is a root-owned mode-0755 x86_64 ELF with resolved glibc/loader dependencies here, and --version passes both ambient and minimal clean environments. This is local host evidence, not guest proof. Current narrow candidate adds a CI-only readiness helper (not in canonical parent ASSETS, preserving existing persistent seed compatibility): bounded direct invocation, then prepare-auth and retry in the exact protected runner environment; preserves exact whole-output version equality. If both fail it emits only exit/classification, UID/HOME metadata, architecture/file format/interpreter description, target/mode/owner/size, npm package version and runtime dependency summary; stdout/stderr are private bounded temp files and never logged. Existing config-tmux and post-reboot checks avoid the failing ambient invocation; the config stage checks exact version, post-reboot protected PTY launch tests runtime/TUI. Existing 20s SSH/60s reboot deadlines and test assertions remain. Sol Medium final review PASS after resolving persistent-seed, exact equality, protected-env, and reboot-probe deadline concerns. Local: Bats 106/106; vm-parent-supervisor 52/52; all vm-parent suites, launch 1/1, OAuth 18/18, browser-auth 37/37; generated cloud config/embedded shell, helper against local pinned CLI, bash syntax, ShellCheck, Python compile and diff checks pass. No guest run locally. Hosted complete Change A remains pending; A1-A5 unchanged and pending.
